newsitem.title: INDIA: BZW, MORGAN, FLEMING TO MANAGE GAIL GDR.
newsitem.headline: BZW, MORGAN, FLEMING TO MANAGE GAIL GDR.

text.p: Merchant banks BZW, Morgan Stanley and Robert Fleming-Jardine Fleming will manage Gas Authority of India Ltd's (GAIL) planned issue of Global Depository Receipts (GDRs), the government said on Tuesday.

The Finance Ministry confirmed in a statement that HSBC Capital Markets India Pvt Ltd, DSP-Merrill Lynch and Goldman Sachs will be joint global coordinators of the $800-million proposed GDR issue by state-owned telecom company Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd (MTNL).
Last month the government said it planned to sell stakes in four firms -- GAIL, MTNL, Indian Oil Corp and Container Corp of India.
It said it planned to sell up to 25 percent of GAIL, which would reduce the government's stake in the gas monopoly to 71.63 percent.
The Divestment Commission had recommended that the government sell 47 million existing MTNL shares and issue 60 million new ones, cutting its stake to 52.6 percent from 65.73.
The privatisation drive is planned partly through an offer of GDRs (GDRs) to overseas investors.
The size of each will depend on final pricing, but a merchant banker last week said he expected a $700-million GDR issue by GAIL and another $800-million offering by MTNL.
The government has set a revenue target of 48 billion rupees ($1.3 billion) from its programme to sell partial stakes in state firms in 1997/98 (April-March).
GAIL is the government gas monopoly and MTNL runs telephone services in Bombay and Delhi.
